newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 4.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Dow Jones industrials fell 39.66 points to 6,477.35, as investors awaited Friday's goverment report on March employment.
* USX's US Steel is looking for prospective acquisitions, merger or partnerships, the unit's president told analysts.
* Coca-Cola Amatil intends to buy a unit of the Philippines' San Miguel Corp for stock worth about $2.7 billion.
* Columbia/HCA has set aggressive growth targets for its home-care operation.
* Ford reported a 2.6 percent decline in light vehicle sales in March while Toyota Motor posted a five percent gain in U.S. light vehicle sales.
* The Internal Revenue Service began to take action against trusts it believes were set up to avoid taxes.
* Intel, Microsoft and Compaq will try to convince broadcasters to adopt their digital television standards.
* Lucent Technologies said it expected strong second-quarter sales in its software and wireless divisions and its quarterly profit would be more than double analysts' estimates.
* The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading in Bre-X Minerals because of high volume.
* Howard Stringer, a former CBS broadcasting chief, is in talks to take a top position with Sony Corp of America, people familiar with the negotiations said.
* Lockheed Martin completed a deal to put 10 noncore units into a new company led by Executive Vice President Frank Lanza.
* Sallie Mae officials face a group of dissident directors over running the student-loan services company.
* On Monday, the first big tobacco case set for trial this year starts.
* SunAmerica Inc signed an important new sponsorship deal with NBC Sports.
* Heard on the Street: Amerindo Investment Advisors of San Francisco has been one of the top money managers in the country for the past few years. But lately, it's fallen to earth -- hard.
* Credit Markets: For the first time since last October, the bond market chalked up gains in the days leading up to a monthly employment report.
